expectations.text: Covers AB 2246: repeals/replaces the Age-Appropriate Design Code with a reasonable-steps framework — default ban on profiling minors, opt-in consent structure, dark-pattern prohibitions
expectations.evidence: AB 2246 never appears. The AADC is described as still on the books ("AB 2273: largely enjoined in NetChoice litigation, so enforcement is uncertain") with no mention of its repeal/replacement.

expectations.text: Covers AB 1709: bans addictive features (personalized algorithmic feeds, autoplay, push notifications) for users under 16, with penalties up to $50,000 per affected minor
expectations.evidence: AB 1709 never appears; the response discusses the older SB 976 ("restricts addictive feeds for minors without parental consent") and admits "I cannot confirm which passed" for 2026 bills. No $50,000-per-minor penalty.

expectations.text: Covers the chatbot pair: SB 1119 (companion-chatbot child-safety duties — risk assessments, crisis protocols; core obligations July 1, 2027) and SB 867 (ban on companion-chatbot toys, sunsetting 2031)
expectations.evidence: Neither SB 1119 nor SB 867 appears; only the 2025 law SB 243 ("companion chatbots, effective January 1, 2026") is covered.

expectations.text: Gets effective dates right: January 1, 2027 default for the package (signed September 10, 2026), with SB 1119's later core date
expectations.evidence: No September 10, 2026 package, no January 1, 2027 package default, no July 1, 2027 SB 1119 date; the response states "my knowledge of the 2026 session is incomplete."

expectations.text: Gives compliance advice: age-assurance posture (AB 1856 OS signals), feature audits for under-16 experiences, profiling defaults
expectations.evidence: Age-assurance advice keys off AB 1043 ("Design for receiving age signals under AB 1043 from January 1, 2027"), not AB 1856; no feature audit of under-16 engagement features (only "Audit ad and analytics SDKs"). Compound elements not met.
